questions.question: What does AIDA stand for? Explain each stage briefly.
questions.expected_answer: Attention: make people notice the advert (headline, picture, colour, sound). Interest: hold their attention with relevant information and benefits. Desire: make them want the product (benefits, testimonials, offers, quality). Action: tell them exactly what to do next (call to action with price, place, time).

questions.question: Distinguish between a feature and a benefit and give an example.
questions.expected_answer: Feature: a fact about the product, e.g. the bag holds 20 litres; the muffin contains real blueberries. Benefit: what that feature does for the customer, e.g. carries all your books and sports kit; a fresh, fruity taste in every bite.

questions.question: Design a short AIDA poster for a juice stall at Entrepreneur's Day, labelling each stage.
questions.expected_answer: E.g. A: picture of an ice-cold orange drink, headline 'THIRSTY?'. I: 'Fresh orange juice, squeezed this morning, no fizz, no fuss.' D: 'Ice-cold! Last term we sold 100 cups. 2 for R10, today only.' A: 'Netball court, both breaks, Friday 14 September. Bring cash.' (Accept reasonable designs with all four stages.)
